links.outcome: Environmental cost (energy, carbon, water, abiotic depletion) versus clinical safety score across LLM configurations
links.effect: 2.61 percentage-point increase in clinical safety score corresponded to about 60-fold increase in estimated energy use per million output tokens; extra test-time compute did not consistently improve safety.
links.quote: The results indicate a non-linear trade-off at the upper end of the safety distribution: a 2.61 percentage-point increase in clinical safety score corresponded to an approximately 60-fold increase in estimated energy use per million output tokens.

unlisted_practices: Dynamic model selection or model cascading (routing lower-risk cases to smaller models) to reduce environmental impact while preserving clinical safety
Life-cycle environmental impact estimation of LLM configurations paired with clinical safety benchmark scores

screen.reason: Evaluates the benchmark trade-off between clinical safety scores and environmental resource usage (energy, compute) across 47 LLM configurations; does not test a specific deployment safeguard or intervention.
